subject: Clarify billing behavior when usage exceeds agreed budget / hard-cap options
messages:
From: Alex Thompson <alex.t@veridian.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 07 Oct 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Query: what happens if we blow past our monthly budget? (rate card + cap options)

Hi Jonas,

Quick one as we're finalizing procurement: can you share the hosted API rate card (baseline token rates) and — critically — what Redwood's behavior is if we exceed an expected monthly spend? Two scenarios we care about:

- Soft overrun: brief unplanned spikes during peak testing
- Sustained overrun: customer activity runs 2-3x projected for a week or more

Our procurement lead also asked whether Redwood supports a hard spending cap (suspend service when hit) vs. unlimited overage invoicing. If a cap requires a contract clause or a specific product tier, please call that out.

I've attached a short RFP excerpt with expected traffic patterns (RFP_spec.pdf). Can we get a note on options + ballpark impact on unit rates?

Thanks,
Alex Thompson
Platform Engineering
Veridian Health

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Thompson <alex.t@veridian.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 07 Oct 2025 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Query: what happens if we blow past our monthly budget? (rate card + cap options)

Alex —

Thanks for the RFP excerpt and the clear scenarios. High level answer first, then specifics below.

Summary (short):
- Baseline hosted API rates: see attached Redwood_RateCard_Oct2025.pdf (summary below).
- Default behavior: we alert at 50%/80%/100% of your monthly target and continue serving; overage is billed at the agreed per-token rate unless a commit/discount applies.
- Hard cap: available as an optional contract feature — will suspend new requests once cap is reached (no new tokens generated) but doesn't retroactively credit prior usage. Requires an explicit clause in the SOW and some provisioning lead time for safety.
- Auto-throttle: we can enable soft throttling (rate-limits) for burst protection without fully suspending service.

Details:
1) Rate card (attached): baseline generation rate for the models in your RFP is $0.0008 per generated token and $0.00012 per input token (these are list rates for hosted). Volume discounts and committed capacity change effective unit price.

2) Overage behavior (hosted API):
   - Alerting: configurable webhooks + e-mail at thresholds you define (we recommend 50/80/95).
   - Billing: by default, any usage beyond the monthly committed/expected amount is invoiced at the per-token rate in the contract.
   - Grace controls: we can set automatic throttles once your month-to-date spend hits X% — this reduces QPS to protect budget while keeping the service available.

3) Hard cap (suspend):
   - Legal: must appear as a clause in the SOW describing actions at hard cap and who can re-enable service.
   - Operational: once enabled, hard cap will block generation requests that would exceed the cap; admin re-enable or automated runway window required.
   - Caveat: hard cap protects future spend but does not reverse already invoiced usage.

4) Procurement-friendly option: commit to a monthly minimum (reserved capacity) + discounted overage tiers. This reduces surprise invoices and gives you predictable unit economics.

Next steps: if you'd like, I'll loop in Marissa (sales lead) to outline discounting for a committed amount and a draft SOW with the hard-cap language. Can we do a 30-minute call tomorrow to confirm which model and cap thresholds you want?

Best,
Jonas Weber
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0132

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Thompson <alex.t@veridian.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 08 Oct 2025 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Query: what happens if we blow past our monthly budget? (rate card + cap options)

Alex — copying Jonas and Aditya. Appreciate the clear ask. A couple of practical terms we can offer to make procurement comfortable:

1) Committed monthly minimum + tiered overage discount
   - Example offer for Veridian Health (illustrative): commit to $25k/month of hosted usage; list token rates reduced by 12% on usage within commit. Overage above commit billed at list minus 15% (so you get a better rate on sustained growth).

2) Hard cap as a contractual control
   - We can include a "spend suspend" clause in the SOW. When MTD spend hits the agreed cap, Redwood will reject new generation requests (HTTP 429 with explanatory header).
   - Re-enable flow: a named Veridian admin can request re-enable via the console or a signed approval e-mail.
   - Note: enabling hard cap requires us to coordinate with infra provisioning if you later move to Dedicated capacity; that transition typically needs ~72 hours.

3) Interim guardrails (no contract change required)
   - Enable threshold webhooks and console auto-throttle at 90% to reduce request rates and avoid hitting the hard cap unintentionally.

4) Invoicing reconciliation
   - We will provide daily usage exports and a 30-day reconciliation window for disputed charges; credits can be issued for manifest system errors only (not for legitimate extra usage).

Attachments: I dropped a draft SOW that includes a sample hard-cap clause and an example reconciliation flow (SOW_Draft.docx). If you confirm the commit level, we will produce a DocuSign SOW for signature (see link: https://www.docusign.com/en/link/abc123-sow).

If Veridian needs an explicit SLA for availability while a hard cap is in place, note that a suspend will be treated as a customer-requested outage and is not covered under uptime SLAs.

Happy to hop on a quick call with procurement to align language. Jonas — can you propose times for a 30-min call tomorrow?

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Head of Sales — Enterprise Accounts
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Redwood Inference

From: procurement <procurement@veridian.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 09 Oct 2025 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Query: what happens if we blow past our monthly budget? (rate card + cap options)

Marissa / Jonas — thanks for the clarity. We'll proceed with the following approach unless you flag a blocker:

- Veridian will sign an SOW that includes a hard-cap suspend at $40,000/month (as proposed, the balance will be our committed baseline).
- On suspension, Redwood will return 429s for new generation requests; Veridian engineering will be responsible for handling fallbacks.
- Redwood will provide daily usage exports and an itemized invoice; procurement will reconcile invoices within 30 days.

Two asks before we sign:
1) Add an explicit statement in the SOW that "suspension for hard-cap is an irreversible action until re-enabled by a named Veridian admin" (we understand re-enable is manual but want the language).
2) Confirm that any discount tiers that apply to overage will be applied automatically on the invoice (e.g., the 15% overage discount on committed customers).

If you can update the SOW and share the DocuSign link, we'll route internally.

Thanks,
Procurement Team
Veridian Health
